market_name: Will 3 Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm which direction the market's implied probability moved and whether 2y/10y yields are repricing in the same direction.
time_plan.1h: Check Fed funds futures (SOFR/short-rate) for corroboration; if no move in rates futures, downgrade confidence.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether any macro catalyst (CPI, FOMC minutes, Fed speak) explains the move — if already public, thesis weakens.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate TLT vs 10y yield move; look for continuation or mean reversion.
time_plan.12h: Mark realized TLT return vs expected; note whether prediction-market move led or lagged rates.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of 3 (vs fewer) Fed cuts in 2026 signals a more dovish rate path. Lower expected policy rates lift bond prices, especially long-duration proxies like TLT. Conversely, a drop in the probability would push TLT down. Direction here is stated for a dovish move; the sign flips for a hawkish repricing.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check DXY and EURUSD for confirmation of direction.
time_plan.1h: Compare with short-end rate futures move; FX should track real rate expectations.
time_plan.2h: Screen for competing FX drivers (ECB/BoJ news, risk sentiment) that could dominate.
time_plan.6h: Reassess whether dollar move persisted or reversed.
time_plan.12h: Record realized UUP return vs expectation and note lead/lag vs market signal.

predictions.reasoning: More expected Fed cuts narrow US rate differentials, typically weighing on the dollar. A dovish repricing in this market would nudge UUP lower; a hawkish repricing would lift it. The relationship is real but noisy at a 12h horizon and easily swamped by cross-currency factors.

evidence_used: Market question tracks number of 25bp Fed cuts in 2026, a direct proxy for the expected policy path
Rate-cut expectations map mechanically to bond yields (TLT) and rate differentials (dollar)
12h window and 700bps tradability threshold far exceed plausible liquid-proxy moves from a single probability shift
uncertainty_notes: No direction of the anomaly is given; predictions are stated for a dovish (more-cuts) move and flip sign for a hawkish one
Fed-path repricing usually happens gradually and is often already reflected in rates futures, limiting leakage edge
Expected magnitudes (20-40 bps) are far below the 700bps tradable threshold — this is not a tradable signal
The 'military_conflict' topic tag appears mislabeled; content is purely monetary policy

llm_justification.summary: This market's implied probability of 3 Fed cuts in 2026 is a proxy for the expected US policy-rate path. A sharp dovish repricing (higher odds of more cuts) would lift long-duration Treasuries (TLT) and weigh on the dollar (UUP); a hawkish repricing flips both signs. The mappings are directionally sound but mechanically weak over a 12h window, with expected moves well under the 700bps tradable bar, so this is research-grade, not tradable.
key_assumptions: A move in this market reflects genuine shift in Fed-path expectations rather than thin-market noise
TLT and UUP retain their standard sensitivity to rate expectations over the window
The prediction-market move leads or coincides with, rather than lags, moves in rates futures
failure_modes: The rate expectation is already fully priced into bonds/FX, so no incremental move occurs
The prediction-market shift is illiquid noise unrelated to real Fed expectations
Long-horizon (2026) cut expectations are dominated by data releases that swamp any leakage signal
Dollar and bond moves driven by competing macro factors (foreign central banks, risk sentiment), breaking the proxy
The probability could reverse quickly, whipsawing the direction
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
